$comment: When the next thing said in a conversation resolves the request that is
waiting on it — and when it must not (M66).
A wrong match here approves an action the person did not confirm, so the
rules prefer asking again over guessing: an ACTION is only ever approved
by a whole utterance that is one of `affirmations`, and only ever denied by
one of `denials`; a QUESTION with choices is answered by a choice the words
pick out uniquely; a free-text question takes the words as they are. A
request raised by a turn that had read untrusted content is never resolved
by voice (`tainted`) — the banner is the one surface that shows where the
question's words came from, so that is where it is answered.
Read by jarvis-core/tests/test_spoken_answers.py, which holds the lists in
jarvis/llm/spoken_answers.py equal to these and runs every case. The phone
does not share this logic: an answer said to the phone is sent to the
server as a turn and decided here.

normalisation.letters_digits_only: every other character becomes a space; apostrophes are dropped, so don't and dont are the same word
normalisation.edge_fillers_note: removed from either end, repeatedly, before the lists are consulted; never from the middle, so 'yes please turn it on' is not 'yes'

stopwords_note: dropped from an utterance before its words are matched against a question's choices; what is left must all sit inside exactly one choice

rules.no_pending: Nothing waits on this conversation: the turn is an ordinary turn (`none`).
rules.tainted: Any pending request raised after untrusted content was read is never resolved by words. If the utterance would have resolved it, the decision is `tainted` and the turn says the request waits on the banner; the request is left exactly as it was.
rules.several_pending: More than one request waiting: an affirmation or a denial cannot be attributed, so the decision is `ambiguous` (the turn says what is waiting and asks which); anything else is `none`. Nothing is guessed.
rules.action: One action waiting (no `answerable`): the whole normalised utterance is one of `affirmations` → `approve`; one of `denials` → `deny`; anything else → `none`, and the request keeps waiting. 'yes and also turn on the lamp' is not a yes.
rules.question_with_choices: One question waiting with choices: a denial → `deny` (dismissed). The utterance equal to a choice, or containing a choice as a whole phrase, or whose non-stopword words all appear in exactly one choice → `answer` with THAT choice's exact text (never the utterance). An affirmation answers a choice that is itself an affirmation, likewise a denial. Words that fit two choices, or none → `none`.
rules.question_free_text: One question waiting with no choices: a denial → `deny`; anything else → `answer` with the utterance verbatim (trimmed, not normalised — a URL is an answer).
rules.answer_writes_one_argument: An answer only ever reaches the one argument the tool named in `Tool.answerable`; an approval carries no words at all. That is `approve_request`'s rule, unchanged.
